supported_interpretation: At this checkpoint C shifts computation to different destinations and usually uses maximum CPU frequency. The measured result is faster service for commonly completed tasks and a modest net completion gain, alongside substantially higher CPU energy and some exclusive failures after offloading. This is a joint scheduling observation, not proof that a feature, offloading, or high frequency alone caused the difference.
